# All active projective circuits and the optimized covariance alternative

This is a necessary condition, not a proof of OC. It extends
`candidate a1faf3121382f376` to several deepest bases.
The explicit C2 cap-profile hypothesis remains in force. In particular,
no approximation through supporting-facet coincidences is asserted.
The statement is root-derived and still needs independent audit.

## 1. Setting and notation

Let P be a finite base, and let K_p be positive actual d-dimensional
fibers, d>=1. Let mu be their sum of volume measures, M its mass,
and beta their maximum normalized depth. Assume this family is a
local minimum on its orbit under positive affine projective
denominators L. Pulling the image measure back to the original fibers
gives density L(p)^(-d); all containing halfspaces and candidate points
correspond exactly. The image base generally is not an integer lattice.

Select finitely many critical cap circuits indexed by i=1,...,s,
with at least one circuit at every deepest base. Circuit i passes
through an interior maximizing point (p_i,x_i), and its caps are

    H_ij={a_ij.p+u_ij.x>=b_ij},  |u_ij|=1,
    mu(H_ij)=Q=beta M.

There are rho_ij>0 with sum_j rho_ij=1 and sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0.
These caps cover the entire p_i fiber plane. Fixed strictly cheaper
whole-plane circuit covers are retained at all nondeepest bases.
Existence and persistence of those covers is the critical-cover
input proved in the separately archived source.

Put delta_ip=p-p_i, T_ijp=b_ij-a_ij.p, and assume the functions

    F_ijp(t)=|K_p intersect {u_ij.x>=t}|

are C2 near T_ijp, including constant profiles for strict full or
empty cuts. At these thresholds write

    S_ijp=-F_ijp', R_ijp=-F_ijp'', S_ij=sum_p S_ijp>0,
    kappa_ij=(rho_ij/S_ij)/(sum_l rho_il/S_il).

A cap is minimizing among containing halfspaces through (p_i,x_i).
Its integer-normal first and second derivatives therefore give

    sum_p S_ijp delta_ip=0,
    H_ij^*=-sum_p R_ijp delta_ip delta_ip^T >=0.       (1)

Also define

    V_ij=sum_p S_ijp delta_ip delta_ip^T >=0,
    h_ij=sum_p R_ijp delta_ip,
    k_ij=-sum_p R_ijp.                               (2)

All vectors and matrices may be restricted to the affine base's
linear span. The zero-dimensional case uses zero vectors and matrices.

## 2. First-order circuit functions

For an affine scalar function A on the base, put

    m_A=int A(p)dmu,
    B_ij(A)=-d int_(H_ij) A(p)dmu,
    t_i(A)=sum_j kappa_ij B_ij(A),
    g_i(A)=t_i(A)+d beta m_A.                       (3)

Thus g_i is the raw first derivative of circuit mass minus beta
times total mass. Constant A give g_i(A)=0. The exact common-mass
quantile construction, with rho-weighted threshold displacement zero,
provides a circuit mass tau_i(t) with derivative t_i(A) when
L_t=1+t A. It also gives an upper bound on depth at that whole fiber
plane. Consequently local minimality implies

    max_i g_i(A)>=0 for every affine A.              (4)

Equivalently, zero belongs to the convex hull of the linear functionals
g_i: if it did not, strict separation of that finite convex hull would
give one A making every g_i(A)<0, contradicting (4).

Fix any A such that max_i g_i(A)=0, and put

    I_0(A)={i:g_i(A)=0}.

Call these the groups active to first order in this direction. Every
positive convex dependence among the g_i is supported on I_0(A),
because its evaluation at A is a sum of nonpositive terms equal to zero.
There is therefore at least one such dependence supported on I_0(A).

## 3. Second-order motion and exact common-mass covers

Let B be another arbitrary affine scalar function, and take the path

    L_t(p)=1+t A(p)+(t^2/2)B(p).                      (5)

It is positive at every p for sufficiently small |t|. Choose arbitrary
integer-normal velocities c_ij, independently for every cap. Replace
a_ij by a_ij+t c_ij and b_ij by

    b_ij+t c_ij.p_i+s_ij(t).

The equation sum_j rho_ij s_ij(t)=0 preserves the entire p_i-plane
cover exactly. The C2 implicit-function theorem chooses all s_ij(t)
so the moving caps have a common mass tau_i(t). Its invertible
linearization uses only S_ij>0. More explicitly, the homogeneous
linearized equations are -S_ij ds_ij-dtau_i=0 together with
sum_j rho_ij ds_ij=0; these force dtau_i=0 and every ds_ij=0.

The first threshold velocities are

    v_ij=(B_ij(A)-t_i(A))/S_ij,                     (6)

independent of c_ij by (1). Write A(p)=A(p_i)+b.delta_ip;
the vector b is common to every i.

For i in I_0(A), differentiating twice and subtracting beta times
the total mass derivative gives

    (tau_i-beta M)''(0)
       =g_i(B)+N_i(A,c_i),                          (7)

where

    N_i(A,c_i)
      =d(d+1)[sum_j kappa_ij int_(H_ij) A^2 dmu
                                      -beta int A^2 dmu]
       +sum_j kappa_ij [k_ij v_ij^2
             +c_ij^T H_ij^* c_ij-2 c_ij.w_ij],

    w_ij=d V_ij b-v_ij h_ij.                        (8)

To verify (7), the derivative of the density in (5) is -d A and
its second derivative is d(d+1)A^2-d B. The threshold in the p fiber
has first derivative v_ij-c_ij.delta_ip. Multiplying the profile and
density expansions gives, apart from the second threshold velocity,

    d(d+1) int_(H_ij) A^2-d int_(H_ij) B
       +2d sum_p A(p)S_ijp(v_ij-c_ij.delta_ip)
       -sum_p R_ijp(v_ij-c_ij.delta_ip)^2.

The kappa-weighted second threshold velocities cancel because
kappa_ij S_ij is proportional to rho_ij. The terms with A(p_i)
cancel by sum_j kappa_ij S_ij v_ij=0. The rest is exactly (7)-(8).
The B terms combine to g_i(B). No derivative of a selected center
or of the actual maximum-depth function is used.

For i outside I_0(A), g_i(A)<0 already decreases its comparison
budget to first order for t>0. If the right side of (7) were strictly
negative for every i in I_0(A), all circuit bounds, and the previously
slack covers at nondeepest bases, would be strictly below beta for
small positive t. This contradicts local minimality. We have proved

    max_(i in I_0(A)) [g_i(B)+N_i(A,c_i)]>=0
                   for every B and all c_ij.         (9)

In deriving (9) one may work with the raw differences tau_i-beta M.
Their signs are the signs of the normalized comparison differences,
so no normalization derivative is lost. On I_0(A) those raw
differences have zero first derivative as well as zero initial value.

## 4. Optimize all integer normals, then use the finite alternative

Let J(A) be the groups i in I_0(A) for which

    w_ij belongs to range(H_ij^*) for every j.         (10)

For such a group define the finite real number

    n_i(A)=d(d+1)[sum_j kappa_ij int_(H_ij) A^2 dmu
                                         -beta int A^2 dmu]
         +sum_j kappa_ij [k_ij v_ij^2
                   -w_ij^T (H_ij^*)^dagger w_ij].    (11)

The dagger is the inverse on the range and zero on the nullspace.
By positive semidefiniteness in (1), completing the square gives

    min_(c_i) N_i(A,c_i)=n_i(A),  i in J(A).           (12)

If i is not in J(A), there is a cap and a null vector of H_ij^*
having nonzero product with w_ij. Sending that c_ij along the null
vector makes N_i arbitrarily negative. Such changes are independently
available for each group; only a finite value is needed to obtain a
strict descent. Thus (9) implies that J(A) is nonempty and

    max_(i in J(A)) [g_i(B)+n_i(A)]>=0 for every B.    (13)

Indeed, otherwise first choose B making all finite entries negative,
then their minimizing c_i, and finally finite c_i values making all
remaining groups negative too. If J(A) is empty, the last step alone
contradicts (9).

Here is the precise finite alternative applied to (13). For finitely
many linear functionals l_i and real numbers q_i, if the affine space

    { (q_i+l_i(B))_i : B arbitrary }

misses the open negative orthant, separation of that convex affine
space from the open orthant gives a nonzero vector pi>=0. Its pairing
with the space must be constant: otherwise scaling B with either sign
would make the pairing arbitrarily negative. Thus sum pi_i l_i=0,
and separation from all strictly negative vectors gives sum pi_i q_i>=0.
Normalize sum pi_i=1. Conversely, these two equations preclude every
coordinate being strictly negative. This proves the alternative,
without an interchange of unbounded optimization operations.

Applying it proves the all-active necessary condition: for every A
with max_i g_i(A)=0, there are pi_i>=0, i in J(A), such that

    sum_i pi_i=1,
    sum_i pi_i g_i=0 as a linear functional,
    sum_i pi_i n_i(A)>=0.                            (14)

In particular, groups failing even one range condition (10) cannot
receive positive mass in this second-order certificate for A. The
weights in (14) may depend on A and on the selected initial circuits.
There is no claim that one set of weights handles all directions.

## 5. A simultaneous range test on a subspace of first-order ties

Let W be any linear subspace of affine functions on which every g_i
vanishes. Define E(W) to consist of groups i for which the linear map

    A -> w_ij(A) modulo range(H_ij^*)

vanishes on W for every cap j. Then

    0 belongs to conv{g_i : i in E(W)}.              (15)

To prove it, for each i not in E(W), the set of A in W satisfying
all of (10) for that group is a proper linear subspace of W. A finite
union of proper linear subspaces does not cover a real vector space:
for example choose one nonzero linear equation vanishing on each
subspace, and their nonzero product polynomial cannot vanish identically.
Choose A outside this union. Every group lies in I_0(A), and J(A)
is exactly E(W). Now (14) proves (15). If W has dimension zero there
are no groups outside E(W), and (15) reduces to (4).

This is a finite, checkable obstruction involving actual cap section
covariances and Hessians. It is stronger than checking one arbitrarily
chosen deepest group, but is still only necessary. It does not establish
the C2 hypothesis at an arbitrary extremizer, identify this orbit
minimum with a shape minimum, or prove beta>=gamma_d/h(P).
